lessonActivities.title: 10.3 Bare Infinitive
lessonActivities.content: Bare infinitive (no 'to') usually follows verbs of perception and causative verbs: make, let, have, see, hear, feel.
lessonActivities.tips: If action is directly perceived or forced: use bare infinitive.

lessonActivities.title: Bare Infinitive vs To-Infinitive
lessonActivities.content: Compare: 'I made him leave' (bare) vs 'I asked him to leave' (to-infinitive). 'Help' can use both: 'help me clean' / 'help me to clean'.
examples: She helped me carry the bag.
lessonActivities.tips: With common causatives, the bare form is the default when action is caused.

writingActivities.question: Write 4 sentences with bare infinitive after make/let/have.
writingActivities.hint: Example: I made him do it.

writingActivities.question: Write 3 sentences with to-infinitive after ask/want/need/plan.
writingActivities.hint: Compare to the bare infinitive form.

quizActivities.question: Which is correct?
quizActivities.sentence: He let me ___ in the park.

spellingActivities.sentence: They made me clean the room.
I heard her sing the song.
